title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: morphisms X --f--> S --> T, all de Rham cohomology taken relative to T. On the previous page Grothendieck puts a 'Koszul' filtration on K = Rf_*(Ω•_{X/T}), whose graded pieces are Gr^α K ≃ Ω^α_{S/T} ⊗^L Rf_*(Ω•_{X/S})[-α]. The d_1 differentials of this filtration give, in degree α = 0, the Gauss–Manin connection on R^q f_*(Ω•_{X/S}) (formulas (8), (8')). He also uses RΓ(S, K) ≃ RΓ(X, Ω•_{X/T}) = H_DR(X/T).

On this page:

(12) is the resulting 'Leray spectral sequence in de Rham cohomology':
 E_2^{pq} = H^p(S, α ↦ H^q(Ω^α_{S/T} ⊗^L Rf_*Ω•_{X/S})) ⇒ H^{p+q}_DR(X/T).
- The E_2 term is the hypercohomology on S of a complex of abelian sheaves.
- The differential of this complex is the one induced by Gauss–Manin. It is a differential operator, not O-linear.

(12') covers the favourable case where Ω^1_{S/T} is flat (S formally smooth over T). The derived tensor product becomes an ordinary one and the complex is the de Rham complex Ω•_{S/T} ⊗ R^q f_*(Ω•_{X/S}) of the module with integrable connection R^q f_*. So
 E_2^{pq} = H^p_DR(S/T, R^q f_*Ω•_{X/S}).
The symbol H^p_DR makes sense precisely because of the Gauss–Manin connection. He names these 'suites spectrales de Leray (relatives) en cohomologie de De Rham'.

Application (13)–(14). Take ξ ∈ H^n_DR(X/T).
- Its edge image lies in E_2^{0,n}. This is the kernel of the Gauss–Manin map H^0(S, R^n f_*) → H^0(S, H^n(Ω^1_{S/T} ⊗^L Rf_*)), i.e. the horizontal sections.
- His NB notes that this image is always horizontal (E_∞^{0,n} ⊂ E_2^{0,n}).
- Now suppose the image of ξ in H^0(S, H^n_DR(X/S)) vanishes, i.e. ξ is fibrewise zero. Then (next page) ξ lies in the next filtration step and defines η ∈ E_∞^{1,n-1} ⊂ E_2^{1,n-1}.
- In the flat case η ∈ H^1_DR(S/T, R^{n-1}f_*). He then interprets η as an isomorphism class of torsors P under R^{n-1}f_* equipped with an 'affine connection' d_P: P → Ω^1 ⊗ R^{n-1}f_*. Here d_P is compatible with Gauss–Manin and has values in the cocycles.
- Equivalently, η is the class of an extension of (O_S, d) by R^{n-1}f_* as modules with integrable connection.

Purpose: build the secondary invariant of a fibrewise-trivial class, the de Rham analogue of a normal function / Manin-type invariant. This leads to the Picard–Fuchs / inhomogeneous-equation theme of the dossier.
errors: In the added formula for E_2^{0,n} (and in the NB) the manuscript writes Ω^1_{X/S} ⊗^L Rf_*(Ω•_{X/S}). By (12) it must be Ω^1_{S/T}: the target of Gauss–Manin. This is a slip of the pen.

Gap: the E_2 term as hypercohomology on S of the complex of cohomology sheaves α ↦ H^q(Gr^α) does not come out of the naive spectral sequence of the filtered complex RΓ(S, K). That sequence has E_1 = H^{p+q}(S, Gr^p K). Getting (12) needs a refinement, such as combining with the canonical filtration τ on Rf_*Ω•_{X/S} (a Deligne décalage-type argument). It also needs Gauss–Manin to respect that filtration, which is clear in the flat case but not argued in general. The 'recette générale' invoked on the previous page is not spelled out.
The comparison RΓ(S, Rf_*Ω•_{X/T}) ≃ H_DR(X/T) used on the previous page needs the usual quasi-coherence and finiteness hypotheses. None are stated.

ideas.what: Leray spectral sequence in de Rham cohomology for X→S→T: E_2^{pq} = H^p_DR(S/T, R^q f_* Ω•_{X/S}) ⇒ H^{p+q}_DR(X/T), with Gauss–Manin as coefficient connection, obtained from the Koszul filtration.
ideas.modern_name: Katz–Oda (Leray) spectral sequence for relative de Rham cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Katz and T. Oda (1968), building on Manin (1958) and Grothendieck's suggestions
ideas.where_published: Katz–Oda, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 1968; Katz, Publ. IHES 39 (1970).

ideas.what: Version without smoothness of S/T, using derived tensor products Ω^α_{S/T} ⊗^L Rf_* and hypercohomology of the complex of cohomology sheaves.
ideas.modern_name: Gauss–Manin for non-smooth bases / derived de Rham setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (cotangent complex, derived de Rham) and Berthelot (crystalline); later derived de Rham work (Bhatt and others)

ideas.what: A class fibrewise zero gives η ∈ H^1_DR(S/T, R^{n-1}f_*), read as a torsor with affine integrable connection, i.e. an extension of (O_S, d) by R^{n-1}f_* in modules with connection.
ideas.modern_name: Extension class / infinitesimal invariant of a normal function; Manin map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Manin (1963, function-field Mordell), Griffiths (normal functions, infinitesimal invariant), Carlson (extensions of mixed Hodge structures)

ideas.what: Edge map: the image of H^n_DR(X/T) in H^0(S, H^n_DR(X/S)) is horizontal for Gauss–Manin.
ideas.modern_name: Global classes give flat sections (theorem of the fixed part, easy direction)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the Leray/Gauss–Manin spectral sequence and the secondary invariant η for non-smooth S/T. He uses Ω^α_{S/T} ⊗^L Rf_* and, on the next page, stratifications / P^∞ in characteristic 0. He thus treats η as an extension class even when Ω^1_{S/T} is not flat. This general framework is only sketched. Its full treatment came later through crystalline and derived de Rham methods, not from these notes.
missed.quote: Dans le cas favorable Ω•_{S/T} plat, (il suffit Ω^1_{S/T} plat ...) ... devient (12')
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a modest historical point: an early sketch of normal-function and extension invariants over singular bases. Specialists know the content from later derived de Rham and crystalline work.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean sketch of the Katz–Oda Leray spectral sequence and of the standard construction of the extension class of a fibrewise-trivial de Rham class, as in Manin and Griffiths. The derived/non-smooth formulation is a nice touch but is anticipated by later literature. Nothing here would genuinely surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: In (13) and the NB, the manuscript reads Ω^1_{X/S}, but the mathematically intended object is Ω^1_{S/T}.

'les suites spectrales (12) ... s'appelle suite spectrale de Leray relative' should read roughly 'Comme de juste, les suites spectrales (12) (dans (12')) s'appellent suites spectrales de Leray relatives, en cohomologie de De Rham'. The phrase 'suites spectrales de Leray' is underlined.
The marginal insertion '(il suffit Ω^1_{S/T} plat, i.e. DL-grad [?])' is illegible at the end. It probably means 'i.e. S formellement lisse sur T', matching the previous page.
'Application Soit une [?] classe [?], et soit' probably reads 'Application. Soit une classe, et soit'.
'(12.2 [?]) l'expression H^p_DR [?] un sens' is probably 'où l'expression H^p_DR a un sens, grâce à la connexion de Gauss-Manin de R^q f_*(Ω•_{X/S})'. '(12.2)' is likely a misread of 'où'.
Under (14) the inserted 'H^n_DR(X/S)' is a gloss: Grothendieck notes R^n f_*(Ω•_{X/S}) = H^n_DR(X/S).
